newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algeria says president killer to be executed.
newsitem.headline: Algeria says president killer to be executed.

text.p: Algeria's High Court upheld the death sentence against a former security forces officer who was found guilty of killing president Mohamed Boudiaf in 1992, lawyers said on Wednesday.

"The high court rejected the defence appeal seeking a retrial of the defendant," one of the lawyers said. The lawyers appealed to the high court in the hope to win a retrial arguing their defendant did not get a fair trial.
The High Court announced the confirmation of the death sentence against 31-year-old Lembarek Boumaarafi in a hearing on Tuesday, they added.
An Algiers court condemned Boumaarafi in June 1995, finding him guilty of shooting Boudiaf in the back while the president was addressing an official meeting in the eastern city of Annaba.
Boudiaf's widow Fatiha dissmissed the idea that Boumaarfi was the lone killer saying she believed Boudiaf fell victim of a plot.

Boudiaf returned from 18 years of exile to head the Algerian state in January 1992 when the country plunged into violence after the authorities then cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
Algeria executes those sentenced to death by firing squad.
